key_insight: Finite element optimization of silicon nitride stressor patterns can produce a silicon crystalline undulator with near-sinusoidal sub-mm deformation and nanometer-scale amplitude.
engineering_relevance: This shows a simulation-to-fabrication workflow for designing crystal-based radiation sources that could generate 5–15 MeV gamma photons for 5–30 GeV beams.
method: Modelled stressor-layer-induced deformation with FEM on a silicon (110) substrate
Tuned substrate thickness and undulator period to maximize uniform sinusoidal bending
Fabricated a 160 µm-thick device with 10 periods and 334 µm pitch
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a fabricated undulator with uniform deformation extending up to 20 µm from the surface and design targets validated through simulation-driven parameter refinement.
watch_item: Performance may be sensitive to fabrication tolerances because higher harmonics and nonuniform deformation can reduce channeling quality and radiation efficiency.
paper_title: From Simulation to Fabrication: Realizing Silicon Crystalline Undulators with Silicon Nitride Stressor Layer Patterning
